(TRIVALENT)"}],"comment":"The Ø6 H7 and Ø14 H7 holes carry tight ISO fits on a part that is zinc plated, but the drawing does not state whether the plating thickness is allowed for or if the holes are to be re-machined after coating. Without this allowance the plated holes will be undersize and mating pins or shafts will not assemble. The designer should add a note specifying that the H7 tolerances apply after plating, or that the holes are to be finished after surface treatment.","recommended_correction":"Add a note such as 'H7 TOLERANCES APPLY AFTER PLATING' or 'RE-MACHINE HOLES TO H7 AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT'."},{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"--"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE:- 1) PROFILE CUTTING SHOULD BE DONE. 2) TO BE CASE CARBURISING DONE. 2) TO BE INDUCTION HARDENED UPTO 50 ~ 55 HRC. 3) CASE DEPTH 0.8~ 1.2 mm."}],"comment":"The title block heat treatment field shows '--', contradicting note N3 which requires case carburising and induction hardening, and the notes do not clearly define at which manufacturing stage each treatment applies relative to machining and plating. This ambiguity can cause the shop to skip treatments or apply them in the wrong sequence, resulting in incorrect hardness or distorted features. The designer should fill the title block heat treatment field with the required processes and revise note N3 to explicitly state the order of operations (e.g., machine, carburise, finish-machine, induction harden, plate).","recommended_correction":"Update the title block heat_treatment field from '--' to reflect the required treatments, and rewrite note N3 to specify the exact process sequence and the stage each treatment applies at."}]}
